purpose: Per CEO R301 P0: P-16 anatomical power-transfer experiment. Corrected diffuse transmittance model.
constitutional_basis: Article XXVII (thresholds with provenance). Article XXIX (separate model error from mechanism failure — initial ballistic model was WRONG, diffuse model is correct).

critical_correction.initial_model: Ballistic Beer-Lambert with total attenuation coefficient (mu_a + mu_s) gave ZERO power. This was a MODEL ERROR — total scattering coefficient is 100-200 cm⁻¹ which makes exp(-200*1.5) ≈ 0.
critical_correction.corrected_model: Diffuse transmittance using mu_eff = sqrt(3 * mu_a * (mu_a + mu_s')). Where mu_s' = mu_s * (1-g) is the REDUCED scattering coefficient (g=0.9 anisotropy for tissue, so mu_s' = 0.1 * mu_s). This accounts for scattered photons reaching the detector.
critical_correction.constitutional_principle: Article XXIX: the initial model FAILURE was an implementation error, not a mechanism failure. The mechanism (NIR through skull) is FEASIBLE when correctly modeled.

tissue_optical_properties.model: Diffuse transmittance: T = exp(-mu_eff * d) where mu_eff = sqrt(3 * mu_a * (mu_a + mu_s'))
tissue_optical_properties.reduced_scattering: mu_s' = mu_s * (1 - g) = 0.1 * mu_s (scattering is forward-directed, so effective scattering is 10x less than total)

verdict.status: FEASIBLE — P-16 transcranial NIR power delivery is FEASIBLE under the corrected diffuse transmittance model
verdict.best_wavelength: 940nm for NIR-I (744 μW from 1cm² receiver, 7.4x margin over 100 μW requirement) or 1064nm for NIR-II (3865 μW, 38.7x margin)
verdict.key_finding: The skull transmits 8-55% of NIR light at 850-1550nm under diffuse transmittance (not 0.000% as the ballistic model incorrectly suggested). The initial 'INFEASIBLE' conclusion was a MODEL ERROR.
verdict.p_tech_update: 0.25 → 0.45 (upgraded). The physics is feasible. Multiple wavelengths deliver sufficient power. Even the smallest receiver (0.25cm²) at 940nm delivers 186 μW (1.9x margin over 100 μW).
verdict.tev_update: 0.45 × 0.50 × $275K − $5K = $56,875 (upgraded from $29,125). P-16 moves up significantly in portfolio ranking.
caveats: Model uses diffuse transmittance approximation (valid for thick, highly-scattering tissue). Actual transcranial transmittance may differ.
Thermal load at skin surface: 100-500 mW/cm² (within ANSI Z136.1 skin MPE for chronic exposure). Need thermal modeling.
PV efficiency at 940-1550nm requires specialized cells (GaAs for 940nm, InGaAs for 1300-1550nm). Si is transparent >1100nm.
Angular misalignment, skull thickness variation (5-15mm), and scalp pigmentation are not yet modeled.

existing_technology.what: Subcutaneous PV at 850nm, 17% Si, 31% GaAs efficiency
existing_technology.gap: P-16 goes THROUGH SKULL, not just skin
P-16 is transcranial (skull is thicker and more attenuating than skin)

existing_technology.what: Nanoscale photovoltaic devices through intact mouse brain/skull
existing_technology.gap: Mouse skull is ~0.5mm. Human skull is 10mm. 20x thicker.

existing_technology.what: Transcutaneous NIR rechargeable pacemaker battery at 810nm
existing_technology.gap: Chest wall is different from skull. P-16 targets skull specifically.

existing_technology.what: Wireless deep-brain neuromodulation using NIR-II photovoltaics
existing_technology.gap: Research-stage. P-16 would need to demonstrate chronic implantable feasibility beyond research demos.

P1_prior_art_comparison.strongest_prior_art_argument: Existing technology demonstrates subcutaneous NIR PV (LITERATURE_VERIFIED). Mouse-scale transcranial NIR PV has been demonstrated (Nature Biotech 2025). But chronic transcranial NIR PV through HUMAN skull (10mm, not 0.5mm mouse skull) at safe illumination levels for a therapeutic implant has NOT been demonstrated. P-16's potential contribution: demonstrating that the human skull's diffuse transmittance at 940-1064nm is sufficient for chronic implantable sensing — and designing the energy-management control regime that makes intermittent operation clinically useful.

P16_invention_thesis.input: External NIR illumination (940nm or 1064nm) at safety-limited irradiance
P16_invention_thesis.physical_transformation: Diffuse transmittance through scalp (0.5cm) + skull (1.0cm) → implantable PV receiver
P16_invention_thesis.output: Electrical energy stored in capacitor (μW-mW range depending on duty cycle)
P16_invention_thesis.control_law: Adaptive energy management: sensing duty cycle dynamically adapts to fluctuating transcranial optical power (affected by scalp blood flow, skull thickness variation, angular misalignment)
P16_invention_thesis.unexpected_system_benefit: ZERO-BATTERY chronic implantable sensing through intact skull. Patient doesn't need surgery for battery replacement. External NIR illumination can be applied at home (wearable NIR patch).
P16_invention_thesis.technical_contribution: Not 'NIR powers an implant' (that exists subcutaneously). The contribution is: (1) demonstrating human-scale transcranial NIR power delivery is feasible (this model), (2) adaptive energy management for fluctuating transcranial optical power, (3) integration into a specific clinical product (ICP sensing, drug delivery, or neurostimulation).

P3_P15_vs_P16_comparison.verdict: P-15 and P-16 are complementary, NOT duplicates. P-15 is autonomous but low-power (1-10 μW). P-16 is externally powered but high-power (744+ μW). Different use cases: P-15 for ultra-low-power always-on sensing. P-16 for higher-power intermittent sensing or therapeutic delivery. Portfolio diversification is VALID.
